correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives rho_p(e). Every selected exponent vector defines an exact density via CRT. The self-contained integer enumeration reconstructs N, Q from 26,732,160 exhaustive cases; the finite prime sum and strict <3/400 bound use Fraction with an analytic integral for the infinite remainder. After discarding a zero-density smooth set, all acceptable vectors with squarefree tail satisfy the strict inequality. Exact 397N>308Q proves >77%. The numerical program is a finite certificate, not a substitute for the symbolic density argument.

value.rationale: Trudgian posed the exact natural density as a quantitative open problem. The rigorous bound >0.77 improves the previously certified 0.753659844... by more than 1.6 percentage points, covering more than two-thirds of the gap from that bound to the originally reported finite 0.778307 proportion. A rational, replayable threshold this close to observed data is mathematically motivated; no exact-density solution is claimed. This is more than a generic elementary inequality, though still a finite-cylinder estimate.
